rationale: The complete unit:given.unpacking matches the selected Transfer, Bind and Step definitions. unit:given.patterns supplies b and all-fields/distinct-name requirements; the captured transitive units given.classes, given.syntax, given.programs, given.state, given.storage_places, given.resolution, given.evaluation, given.machine and given.steps introduce the field/class/variable names, alpha, slots, S/O/V/nu, class table Delta, expression evaluation, configurations K, statement lists P, domain and binding notation before this rule. Transfer.cons selects a named (field,slot) at any position, removes it before recurring, and emits the same slot paired with its destination; Transfer.nil requires both remaining lists empty. Together with distinct pattern field names and exact stored-versus-declared field order, this gives a permutation of all declared names exactly once. Bind.unpack checks class equality, declaration membership, distinct destination names and freshness against every existing variable key; none-valued existing variables therefore still block reuse. It removes exactly the selected object list entry, prepends exactly the transferred bindings, and preserves all other object entries, old bindings and the counter. Both some object and none slots pass through unchanged, and zero fields remove the container without producing variables. The displayed declaration-order rule is an explicit presentation choice; the source additionally realizes all pattern orders permitted by given.patterns. Step evaluates once using the original Eval and then applies Bind within a single transition, removing exactly the first statement. Bind.variable recovers the preceding Let rule. Neither Eval, Bind nor Step has a hidden WellFormed or typing premise. The finite-map rendering is under given.state's distinct-key convention, while the source defines raw-state operations using explicit list decompositions. No discrepancy was found.
limitations: This is a source correspondence review, not execution of Lean, Cargo, rendering or evidence validation. Lean is responsible for proof correctness; tactic bodies were not independently re-proved.

The review covers this unit and the dependencies needed to interpret it. Conservative full-source snapshots were inspected only where listed in examined; no claim is made about static type safety or correspondence of unpacking with Shared.
